title: Risk First: 3 rules that keep traders alive

strategy.hook: Counter-intuitive claim in the first line: entries are not the problem, sizing is. The crash visual hits on frame one.
strategy.pacing: Three numbered rules, each with one picture and one number. Fast build, then a hushed beat, then the maths payoff.
strategy.retention: 'Here's the part nobody posts' at ~60% re-opens curiosity right before the most surprising number (lose 60% and still profit).
strategy.loop: The close returns to the hook's idea (downside first) and asks for a save, so a replay starts on the crash again.

lines.text: Most traders don't blow up from bad entries. They blow up from bad sizing.
Rule one: risk one percent of your account per trade. Max.
Ten losses in a row? You still have ninety percent. At ten percent risk? About a third.
Rule two: set your stop before you enter. Not after it hurts.
Rule three: only take trades that pay at least twice the risk.
At two to one, you can lose six trades out of ten and still profit.
Protect the downside first. Save this for your next trade.
